prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates a very near foreground—camera wearer’s hand/bottle and nearby machine edges at roughly 0.2–0.6 m—from the standing person at about 1–2 m and the darker rear workshop at several metres. The standing person remains ahead and slightly left-to-centre, while the foreground hand/object shifts across the lower centre/right and stays within the wearer’s arm’s reach; large equipment occupies the middle-right behind it. Across the five frames, the person’s apparent distance changes only modestly, while camera rotation makes him move from left to centre and back toward the left; nearer equipment surfaces sweep more strongly across the view. Depth makes foreground/background ordering and occlusion clearer than RGB, but it is unreliable on thin limbs, object boundaries, the bottle’s reflective/transparent surface, and the dark far background, so metre estimates are approximate.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map consistently isolates the standing person about 1–2 m ahead and another large foreground person-region at the bottom, corresponding largely to the camera wearer’s close hand/arm at about 0.2–0.5 m. It shows that the standing person stays left or near centre relative to the wearer, while the close foreground region overlaps and occludes the lower middle/right of the scene; the two person regions are roughly 1–2 m apart in depth. Across the five frames, the standing mask shifts laterally and changes silhouette as the view and body orientation change, while the wearer’s foreground mask enters, expands, or leaves the lower edge. Instance masks make person extents and occlusion boundaries easier to see than RGB, but the map misses much of the machinery and bottle, merges body parts poorly, and implausibly labels small machine/background regions as “suitcase” or “truck,” so those object identities and extents are unreliable.
descriptions.pose: The pose map places the standing person’s head and torso ahead at roughly 1–2 m, with the wearer’s detected hands much nearer at the lower foreground, within about 0.2–0.5 m; the other person’s hands remain near his torso or extend toward the left/right depending on the frame. The torso geometry suggests that he generally faces approximately toward the camera wearer, with modest turning between frames, although the sparse facial points cannot reliably establish gaze direction. Over time, his skeleton shifts from left to centre and back toward the left as the viewpoint changes, while arm configurations change and one or both hands are intermittently occluded or near the frame boundary. Pose reveals joint layout, body orientation, and hand-to-torso spacing more clearly than RGB, but several limb segments are anatomically distorted, hand keypoints form noisy clusters, and absent lower-body joints prevent reliable statements about legs, full-body distance, or objects around him.
